usageNotes: Appends a new firewall rule to the per-container rule chain for the specified LXC guest; the container-level firewall must be enabled (via the container's firewall options) and the node firewall must also be active for rules to take effect. The caller requires VM.Config.Network on /vms/{vmid}. Rules are inserted at the end by default; supply 'pos' to place the rule at a specific zero-based position in the chain.

examples.summary: Block all inbound traffic on port 23 (Telnet) from any source on container 110

tips: Use 'macro' (e.g. 'SSH', 'HTTP', 'HTTPS') instead of manually specifying proto/dport when targeting well-known services — macros keep rules readable and reduce mistakes.
The 'digest' param can be passed (read from a prior GET of the rules list) to prevent a lost-update race if multiple operators may edit the ruleset concurrently.
For LXC interfaces, 'iface' must match the container's network key name (e.g. 'net0', 'net1') — arbitrary interface names accepted for host rules are NOT valid here.
New rules are inactive until 'enable' is explicitly set to 1; omitting 'enable' creates the rule in a disabled state.
Do not mix IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in a single 'source' or 'dest' value — use separate rules for each address family.
